newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals thin, eye firm dollar.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals thin, eye firm dollar.

text.p: Strong demand for the dollar in thin Monday trade sapped liquidity and kept regional currencies in a mild defensive stance in tight ranges.
"The dollar/yen situation has affected all regionals to a minor extent," a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said, adding that thin volume has failed to move currencies out of tight ranges.
With dollar/yen climbing to 116.18 in Asia today, foreign investors were seen likely to liquidate regional currencies.
The ringgit was marginally weaker with closing of accounts by Kuala Lumpur-based banks and corporates amid a strong dollar environment, possibly leading to further selling.
At 0430 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5290/00 a dollar against 2.5283/93 at the close of Kuala Lumpur trade on Friday.
The Singapore dollar was trapped around Friday's trading band with scant participation from large investors and no central bank activity detected in morning trade.
Dollar/Sing rose to 1.4000 on short-term speculation, later offset by some commercial profit taking, dealers said.
In Thailand, year-end demand for baht and dull dollar/baht trade this morning prompted buying in the local money market.
Dollar/baht eased to 25.639/644 midday Monday against 25.625/630 late on Friday.
The central bank fixed the dollar/baht mid-rate at 25.61 against 25.59 on Friday.
"The two satangs change is nothing to get excited over. It's just in line with the stronger dollar," a Singapore dealer said.
The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar at midday, but overnight dollar deposit rates soared, dealers said.
The dollar remained well-bid against the ruppiah with strength overnight apparently prompted by year-end demand.
Ample liquidity and devaluation fears kept sentiment weak in the longer-term for ruppiah, although profit taking took dollar/ruppiah off the morning's highs.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention rate at 2,358/2,550 and the conversion rate at 2,358/2,406 last Friday.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,363.0/63.50 at 0430 GMT against an opening of 2,363.0/64.25.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen (662) 652-0642 and Jacqueline Wong in Singapore (65-8703088)
